title: a new task's first round never dead-ends: a leftover empty worktree starts fresh, and a first round that needs firstmate (a scope widening, a question) has a channel before any pull request exists
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-30 T-157's first round stopped before any commit (codex could not run git, fixed by T-147). Its worktree and local branch stayed at the old main. The next dispatch reused them as a retry (actor r1b): the prompt told the worker the branch already carried earlier work, the task's spec file was not seeded (T-147 seeds only a new worktree), and the worker stopped again, rightly. firstmate had to remove the empty worktree and branch by hand. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-160.json, is committed on this branch.

When a task has no pull request and its worktree holds no commit beyond the base and no uncommitted change, fm-worker.sh treats the next dispatch as a first round: it recreates the worktree from the current base (or fast-forwards it), seeds the spec as T-147 does, and never says the branch carries earlier work. A worktree that holds commits or changes is kept exactly as today (never discard work). The prompt says 'retry of earlier work' only when there is earlier work.

No-PR channel: on 2026-09-30 T-157's first round needed a scope widening; its spec was already committed on the branch (so fm-worker read the branch copy), no pull request existed (fm-worker opens none for a round that only asked), so firstmate's answer had nowhere to go and the captain had to allow a one-off spec commit. Fix it in fm-worker.sh: a first round that asks (SCOPE-BLOCKED, ASK-*) opens a draft pull request carrying the question, so firstmate can answer and widen scope there as for any round; and a new task's spec in firstmate's repository, when it differs from the branch copy and the branch holds nothing but that spec, is taken from the repository. Test both.

Also (found 2026-10-01 verifying T-157 on the Mac): tests/review.test.sh's CI-wait cases fail on macOS on main (13) and on T-157 (14) while passing on Linux - 'a head whose checks had finished is not waited on', 'past the same bound a required check with no run yet is stated as missing', 'the bound names both the running and the not-yet-created check'. Make them wait on the stubbed gh's state, not on wall-clock polls, so they agree on both hosts; tests/review.test.sh joins this task's scope.

Tests: an empty leftover worktree on an old base is replaced by a fresh one on the current base with the spec seeded and a first-round prompt; a leftover with a commit or an uncommitted change is kept and the prompt says so. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves.
